hints: Look closely at each fatty acid tail in X, Y and Z for kinks. A straight zig-zag means no double bonds, a bent kink means a C=C double bond is present.

Remember saturated means zero C=C bonds, unsaturated means one or more C=C bonds. Then compare the three tails in each triglyceride for length and number of double bonds to judge if they are different.
walkthrough:
**Spot saturated versus unsaturated tails**

Look for double bonds. A straight chain has only single bonds, so it is saturated. A chain with one or more kinks has C=C double bonds, so it is unsaturated.

In X, the top tail is straight but the middle (1 kink) and bottom (3 kinks) are bent. In Y, the middle tail is straight but the top (1 kink) and bottom (2 kinks) are bent. In Z, all three tails are straight with no kinks.

**Decide who contains which type**

X has both a straight tail and bent tails, so it contains saturated and unsaturated fatty acids. Y also has both a straight tail and bent tails, so it also contains both types. Z has only straight tails, so it contains only saturated fatty acids.

**Count how many different fatty acids in each**

Different means different chain length or different number of double bonds. X has three clearly different tails: saturated, mono-unsaturated and poly-unsaturated. Y also has three different tails: mono-unsaturated, saturated and di-unsaturated. Z has only straight saturated tails of very similar type, so it does not have more than two different types.

That gives: saturated in X, Y and Z, unsaturated in X and Y only, more than two different in X and Y only. This matches row A.

options.A: Correct. X, Y and Z all have at least one straight saturated tail. Only X and Y have kinked unsaturated tails. Only X and Y have three different tails.
options.B: False. The middle column is wrong because Z has no kinks or double bonds, so Z contains no unsaturated fatty acids, while X and Y do.
options.C: False. Z is missed from the saturated column and wrongly added to the unsaturated column, but Z is fully saturated with straight chains only.
options.D: False. The first and third columns are wrong because X and Y do contain saturated tails, and Z does not contain more than two different fatty acids.
